mustHave: Apps are private by default; outside users can only connect after sharing is switched on (Distribution > Sharing).
Until Atlassian reviews the app, users see a warning that it has not been reviewed by Atlassian, but they can still proceed.
Atlassian review is optional for going live and Atlassian publishes no review timeline.
Switching on sharing requires a vendor name, a privacy policy URL and a personal-data declaration.
Apps that store personal data must report accounts via the personal data reporting API (every 7 days by default).
There is no API for creating Atlassian OAuth apps; registration is done in the developer console by a human.
offline_access is needed to get a refresh token (with audience=api.atlassian.com).
Refresh tokens rotate and expire after 90 days of inactivity.
Each OAuth app has a single 65,000-point hourly API quota shared across all tenants/sites (since March 2026); exhausting it returns 429 for everyone until the hour resets.
Organisation/site admins can block end users from installing OAuth (3LO) apps.
The callback URL must exactly match the redirect URI; the developer should copy Composio's redirect URI from their Composio auth config rather than from older docs.
Developers choose between an account-level and a resource-level grant when creating the app.
Scopes must be added in the developer console before they can be requested, there is a cap of 50 scopes, and users must re-consent when scopes change.
Composio's sources disagree on (or the guide flags uncertainty about) whether Jira has a Composio-managed OAuth app.
Connections need the Jira site base URL (https://<site>.atlassian.net).
The guide recommends the developer's own app for production with concrete reasons (branding on the consent screen and/or the shared quota).
mustNotSay: That Atlassian approval or review is required before outside users can connect.
That a review or approval duration is an official/published figure.
A hard-coded Composio redirect URI presented as the one to use.
